hlni.insight: Course titles are insufficient to categorize a degree's scope as they are often shared across programs.
hlni.audienceGap: Students assume a module title like 'Business Law' is exclusive to a specific degree.
hlni.viewerChange: Students shift from guessing based on labels to looking for actual curriculum depth.
hlni.support: Logical limitation: a label cannot be used to distinguish categories if it exists in both.
hlni.payoff: The viewer realizes labels are common, shifting the focus to comparing actual curriculum depth.

creativeAngle: A logical challenge debunking the myth that course titles define degrees.
objective: Guide students to look beyond labels when comparing B.Com and BBA.
targetAudience: A broad +2 student audience discovering ideas, courses, or student experiences

shots.name: The Quiz Setup
shots.visual: Host holds a card labelled 'Business Law' with a questioning expression.
shots.dialogue: B.Com or BBA? Identify which degree owns 'Business Law'. Go.
shots.onscreenText: B.Com vs BBA: Guess the Degree

shots.name: The Reveal
shots.visual: A large red stamp 'NOT ENOUGH INFO' slams onto the screen over the card.
shots.dialogue: Subject: Business Law. Degree: B.Com or BBA? Answer: Not enough info.
shots.onscreenText: Subject: Business Law. Degree: B.Com or BBA? Answer: Not enough info.

shots.name: The Insight
shots.visual: Host leans in close to the lens, speaking calmly.
shots.dialogue: Titles overlap. What differentiates the law curriculum between these two? Always check module depth.
shots.onscreenText: What differentiates the law curriculum between these two?

creativeSummary.keyCreativeIdea: A game show challenge proves that single course titles are common and cannot distinguish between B.Com and BBA.

selected.title: The Missing Link Challenge
selected.audienceGap: Assuming a single module name (e.g., 'Business Law') belongs exclusively to one degree.
selected.hlni: One unlabeled example does not prove which category or programme contains it. An exclusive claim needs information that actually links the example to that category.
selected.viewerChange: Recognizes that course titles are insufficient to categorize a degree's entire scope.
selected.concept: A rapid-fire game where the viewer tries to guess the degree based on one subject, only to be shown the 'Not Enough Info' reveal.
selected.device: A game show-style reveal with a 'Not Enough Info' stamp.
selected.support: This is a reasoning limit: absent information cannot establish an exclusive classification.
methodSteps: Present one example without a source linking it to a category.
Separate a plausible guess from what the available information proves.
Identify the exact missing source or information needed to decide.
selected.interpretationRule: Answer not enough information when the necessary link is absent, then name the evidence that would resolve it.
selected.visibleProof: A forced-choice guess is replaced by a justified third answer and a precise request for missing evidence.
selected.payoff: Answer not enough information when the necessary link is absent, then name the evidence that would resolve it.
selected.limitations: Do not assert that the example belongs to both degrees, or to either one, without actual curriculum evidence.

comparedWith.hlni: A task label alone does not tell you what you must produce, what will be assessed, or what feedback you receive. Ask these as separate questions.
comparedWith.device: A split-screen showing a task title vs. a three-column tracker for product, criteria, and feedback.

comparedWith.hlni: A short illustrative activity can reveal where you need help or what you want to investigate next; it cannot determine which degree suits you.
comparedWith.device: A conversation between two friends over a notebook.
